comment: Single source of truth for the on-prem nodes. Terraform reads it to build them and Ansible reads it in Module 03 to generate the inventory, so the two can never disagree. Sizing rationale: docs/adr/0004-onprem-substrate.md.

network.name: platform
network.comment: libvirt NAT network. Each node's address is assigned by cloud-init inside the guest and declared here, so nothing is hand-configured and nothing drifts on reboot. The mac field is reserved for a future switch to libvirt DHCP reservations and is unused today.

loadbalancer.comment: Addresses Cilium hands to type=LoadBalancer Services, announced on the node network by ARP (ADR-0013). These are NOT libvirt's to give: the platform network has no DHCP range at all, so the only addresses in use on this /24 are .1 (the libvirt bridge) and the three nodes. A start/stop block rather than a CIDR, deliberately - a CIDR raises the question of whether its network and broadcast addresses are allocatable (allowFirstLastIPs) and a range does not.
loadbalancer.gateway_comment: The Gateway's address is PINNED out of the pool rather than taken from it, because /etc/hosts points a name at it and a name that moves is worse than no name. Pinned with Gateway spec.addresses[type=IPAddress], which is LB-IPAM aware; the older io.cilium/lb-ipam-ips annotation does the same thing and is documented as heading for deprecation.
loadbalancer.gateway_wildcard_comment: The HTTPS listener and its certificate are WILDCARD, so adding an application to the platform means adding an HTTPRoute and a line in /etc/hosts - not touching the Gateway or reissuing a certificate (ADR-0014). Our own CA can sign a wildcard for a domain we invented, which a public CA could not; that is the one thing a private CA is unambiguously better at.
loadbalancer.gateway_hostnames_comment: Every name that must resolve to the Gateway from this workstation. There is no DNS on this network, so each one needs an /etc/hosts line even though the certificate covers them all - `make hosts` writes them.

kubernetes.comment: Fixed in ADR-0007, before kubeadm ran. Changing either CIDR later means rebuilding the cluster, so they live here where the kubeadm config, the Cilium values and the Ansible roles all read the same number. Neither may overlap the node network above.
kubernetes.version_comment: The Kubernetes version must match what the Packer image installed and held (K8S_MINOR in packer/ubuntu-2404/scripts/30-kubernetes.sh). Ansible's preflight role asserts they agree and refuses to build a cluster if they do not, because a control plane newer than its kubelets is supported in one direction only and obscure when it breaks.
kubernetes.argocd_comment: Two different numbers. argocd_chart_version pins the HELM CHART; the chart decides which Argo CD it installs, and 10.11.0 carries Argo CD v3.5.5. Check both when moving the pin - `helm search repo argo/argo-cd --versions` prints CHART VERSION and APP VERSION side by side - and keep the app version's minor matching the argocd CLI in scripts/install-tools.sh, because a CLI far ahead of its server fails in ways that read like permissions problems.
kubernetes.gateway_api_comment: Gateway API CRDs are a Layer 1 prerequisite of Cilium's Gateway support (ADR-0012), and the one thing in this repository that arrives as a raw URL rather than a Helm chart. So it is pinned by CONTENT as well as by version: the ansible role verifies this sha256 before applying and refuses if it differs, because a version tag is a mutable pointer and a digest is not. To fill it in, run the role once with sha256 empty - it prints the actual digest and the line to paste.
